Application

We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

*Open to hiring remote across the US — we also have offices in New York, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Paris, and Tel Aviv.

We are hiring a Growth Marketing Manager to own paid search and the emerging bidding-platform channels end to end Google Ads today, ChatGPT Ads and whatever bids next. This is a hands-in-the-account role: you build campaigns, run experiments, manage bids and budgets daily, and defend every dollar against our cost-per-subscriber breakeven. You'll manage seven-figure budgets in spend across markets (US + international) and be the person who knows, at any moment, why the number moved.

We're an AI-native creative platform in scale mode. Paid search is one of our priority acquisition channels and we're actively expanding it — new geos, new bidding surfaces, new optimization events. You'll be the operator driving that.

What You'll Do

Day-to-day management of Google Ads and ChatGPT Ads — campaign structure, keywords, bids, budgets, negatives, quality score, geo and device splits.

Own the cost-per-acquisition number. Manage to a cost-per-acquisition target, not clicks or registrations. Know the funnel from impression → registration → subscription and where it leaks.

Run a continuous test roadmap — bidding strategies (tCPA / Smart Bidding), optimization events, ad copy, landing pages, audience and geo splits. One test, one hypothesis, one readout.

Prove incrementality. Design and read geo holdouts, conversion-lift studies, and pause tests. Distinguish incremental subscribers from ones we'd have gotten anyway.

Manage budget across markets — allocate and reallocate spend by market and campaign against performance, break out international blobs, fund the geos that earn it.

Stand up new bidding platforms as they emerge. You'll be first-in on the next channel and write the playbook for it.

Report clearly. Daily and weekly readouts that lead with the "why," not just the table. Partner with our analytics stack, much of this is instrumented and semi-automated; you'll extend it.

Work cross-functionally with creative, lifecycle, product marketing, and engineering on tracking, attribution, and landing page conversion.

What We're Looking For

4+ years managing paid search, with direct ownership of seven-figures in budget.

Deep Google Ads expertise — Smart Bidding, tCPA/tROAS, Performance Max / AI Max, Demand Gen, search term hygiene, quality score, the Editor.

A track record running incrementality tests (geo holdouts, lift studies) and acting on the results — not just reporting platform-reported conversions.

Fluency in funnel economics: CAC, LTV, cost-per-acquisition, payback. You optimize to downstream value, not proxy events.

Comfort in the data — SQL or willingness to learn it, plus GA4 / Mixpanel or equivalent. You pull your own numbers.

Rigorous experiment discipline and clear, opinionated written reporting.

Bonus Points

Subscription / freemium or consumer SaaS experience.

International / multi-market paid search experience.

Experience with MCP / AI tooling to automate redundant tasks such as daily optimizations and reporting.

Early experience with AI-native ad surfaces (ChatGPT Ads, etc.) or other non-Google bidding platforms.

Familiarity with attribution plumbing — click IDs, enhanced conversions, server-side tracking.

The Role

We're looking for a pragmatic Product Manager to lead Kestra's product in the data orchestration domain: how data teams build, run, and monitor pipelines with Kestra, from ingestion and transformation to data-aware orchestration across the tools they already use. You'll take features from customer problem to delivery with minimal process. This is not a "project manager" or "product owner" role; we care about releasing real value fast and won't ask you to maintain SCRUM rituals.

Own the full product lifecycle - understand the problems of data engineers, analytics engineers, and data platform teams; define technical specs; prototype (AI tools encouraged); and work closely with developers to deliver high-quality releases.

Coordinate development progress and ensure features are delivered, QA'd, documented, and ready to go.

Improve the product continuously based on customer feedback, usage data, and community input.

What We're Looking For

Hands-on, startup-minded PM comfortable working without heavy process or structure.

Strong background in the data domain - you've built or managed data pipelines yourself and know tools like dbt, Fivetran or Airbyte, and warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks from hands-on use.

Practical experience with workflow orchestration (Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, or Kestra itself) and a clear understanding of scheduling, backfills, retries, and dependencies between datasets.

Excellent communication and clarity in writing - specs, product decisions, and public-facing documentation.

Full ownership mentality. You iterate quickly based on feedback and don't wait to be told what to do.

Comfortable working with globally distributed teams across time zones.

Past experience as a data engineer or analytics engineer.

Experience moving a team from Airflow (or another orchestrator) to a new platform.

Experience in a B2B software or open-source company.

Exposure to SaaS products, especially self-serve or platform-oriented.

Familiarity with data engineering communities and how they adopt tools.

About Weaviate

Weaviate is an AI startup with open source and creativity at its core. Our AI-native vector database uses machine learning to create meaningful insights from unstructured data in a completely new way. Named one of Forbes’ Top 50 AI startups, and with over a million monthly downloads, Weaviate is quickly growing in popularity with developers and enterprises alike.

Our team members work remotely across the globe with the flexibility to work from anywhere and at any time. Our people experience this as a massive benefit! Operating with a strong sense of ownership and collaboration, our teams prioritize results while empowering each individual to do their best work.

About this role

Weaviate has been really successful in enterprise, and we're doubling down on that by growing our enterprise-facing teams. That shifts what the product has to do. Large customers arrive with specific requirements, and someone has to decide which of those we build, in what order, and which ones we tell the customer we won't build.

As Director of Product, you'll own product strategy and decision-making across the Weaviate Database, Weaviate Cloud, and our agent products. You'll spend a lot of your week with customers, and the rest of it turning what you heard into a roadmap that engineering can act on. You'll work directly with our CTO on vision and with tech leads on what's actually feasible.

This is a player-coach role. You'll manage a small product team, likely one to three PMs over time, while continuing to own product areas yourself.

Who we're looking for

You're comfortable in front of enterprise customers, and you go looking for those conversations rather than waiting for them to be scheduled. You can tell the difference between a request that will block a deal and a request that's a minor annoyance, and you can explain how you reached that conclusion.

You make prioritization decisions using evidence. When you say one feature should ship before another, you can clearly explain the business impact and tradeoffs behind that decision, and you're comfortable defending it.

You have a real working relationship with engineering. You understand that adding something to the plan means something else moves, and you're upfront about those tradeoffs. You take tech debt seriously when engineers make the case for it. You spend enough time with the teams that trust is already there when a hard conversation comes up.

You're senior enough to hold your ground. Priorities will get pulled in different directions by big opportunities, and part of your job is deciding when that's the right call and when to push back.

Responsibilities
Translate Customer Reality into a Roadmap

Run a continuous rhythm of customer conversations: discovery calls, renewals, and support signal

Turn enterprise requirements into clear specs engineering can build from, with the underlying problem attached, so the team can make good calls without you in the room

Maintain one prioritized roadmap that shows what's shipping, what got moved to make room, and why

Own Prioritization and Business Value

Attach an expected business impact to significant roadmap items so tradeoffs can be argued with evidence

Assess incoming enterprise requests for criticality and pattern: is this one customer, or the first of many

Manage expectations across sales, leadership, and customers when priorities change

Define success metrics for major features and follow up on them after they ship

Work Closely with Engineering

Partner with tech leads on sequencing, feasibility, and dependency-heavy work across releases

Make the cost of a change in direction explicit before it lands on a team

Give engineering enough context on customer problems that they can push back with better ideas

Keep the balance between customer-driven work and the reliability and platform work engineering needs to do

Set the Operating Standard for Product

Establish the operating cadence for planning and execution, with conventions engineering teams actually follow

Hire and develop PMs as the team grows, while staying hands-on in your own areas

Partner with GTM and marketing so new capabilities land with positioning that matches the customer problem they solve

Requirements

8+ years in product management, including recent hands-on IC work. You've owned a roadmap yourself, not only through a team

Experience with enterprise customers: discovery, requirements gathering, and expectation management with large accounts

Track record of quantifying the business impact of roadmap decisions and defending prioritization to stakeholders who disagree

Comfortable in a technically deep domain such as databases, data infrastructure, distributed systems, or developer tools. You don't need an engineering background, but you do need to hold your own with tech leads

Experience running product process in Linear or a comparable tool, with a clear opinion on how it should be set up

Strong written communication. Most of our decision-making happens in docs

Some people management experience, or clear readiness to take that step with a team of one to three

Working hours between GMT and ET, with flexibility for an occasional early or late call.

Experience at a developer tools or open source company

Familiarity with vector search, embeddings, RAG, or agent workflows

Background working with enterprise customers alongside a self-serve motion

Experience in a company where product owned both an open source project and a commercial cloud offering

Competitive compensation, including paid time off.

Budget available to spend on going to conferences, co-working space, home office equipment, etc.

Work with very experienced and fun team members.

An atmosphere that encourages learning and personal growth, and that gives you lots of freedom, flexibility, and responsibilities.

You will work at the forefront of search, ML/AI, and cloud-native technologies - and all of it is open source.

Working knowledge of machine and workload identity — service-to-service authentication, non-human identity, service accounts, secrets/key management, and emerging AI-agent access patterns.

Strong security engineering fundamentals across cloud infrastructure security controls in GCP, AWS, and/or Azure, including Kubernetes and cloud control-plane access models.

Familiarity with identity platforms and access tooling (e.g., Okta, JIT/access-orchestration tooling) and how access controls are enforced in production.

Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with a data-driven approach to decision-making.

Experience running long-term, complex security programs that deliver iterative, measurable risk reduction.

Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to influence and lead without direct authority across engineering and security teams.
